newsitem.title: USA: Apria sees Q3 earnings below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Apria sees Q3 earnings below forecasts.

text.p: Apria Healthcare Group Inc said on Tuesday it expects to report third quarter net income between $0.38 and $0.42 per share on a fully diluted basis, below analysts' expectations.
Analysts had forecast the company would earn $0.46 a share, according to First Call. Last year, the company earned $0.37 a share in the third quarter.

"While the company's projection for 1996 is below the First Call consensus estimates, it represents earnings growth of approximately 17 percent, compared to the prior year," said Jeremy Jones, chief executive officer.

Apria, the nation's largest integrated home healthcare provider, expects revenues for the third quarter ending September 30 to be up about 10 percent from the year ago's $277.6 million, it said in a statement.
Apria expects net income for the year ending December 31 of between $1.62 and $1.66 per fully diluted share, excluding the impact of a merger with Vitas Healthcare Corp.
That figure is well below analysts' estimates of $1.77 a share, according to First Call. In 1995, Apria earned $1.40 per diluted share before one-time charges.
For 1996, net revenue is expected to rise 8 percent from last year's $1.1 billion.

The company attributed the reduced revenue and earnings expectations to its nationwide information systems conversion, which disrupted normal business operations and service levels, and caused revenue adjustments during the third quarter.

Debt levels, excluding the Vitas acquisition, are expected to remain stable in the third quarter and decline slightly through the balance of 1996. Debt rose $120 million in the first half of the year.
Accounts receivable are also expected to trend downward toward the end of 1996, he added.
Apria plans to release results for the third quarter in late October.
